brief: GS's Callahan flags reserved optimism: NDX has risen 7 of 8 sessions to new highs and SPX has beaten the equal-weight index in 18 of 21 sessions, but GS's sentiment indicator is firmly negative and market breadth (median stock 16% below its 52-week high) is at its lowest level since 2000/the dot-com bubble. GS is unsure whether the rally is bottoms-up (Muse, personal agents, model updates, ROIC confidence) or macro-led (rates, oil post-FOMC). Within tech, CPU semis INTC and AMD (each +35%+ in September) are outperforming NVDA (+2%) and AVGO (-5%, now below its 200-dma and at a 1-2x fwd P/E discount to NVDA), while inference-economy names like Cloudflare extend gains; broader Semis are down 11% in Q3 but up four straight weeks, with SOX valuation inversely tied to oil. MU reports Wednesday with balanced positioning; ACN reports Thursday, with GS modeling a cautious FY27 guide (3-4% CC growth, 6-8% EPS growth) amid AI-disruption fears. TTWO sits near 10-year lows versus the S&P 500 ahead of GTA 6. The week ahead brings JOLTS, PCE, ISM and NFP data.
